title: uuencoding/src/decode.rs 'end' detection does case-insensitive compare but scan.rs is_end_line() also does — comment says 'lowercase' vs reality
description: In uuencoding/src/decode.rs lines 116-121, the 'end' line check allocates a lowercased vec and compares to b'end'. In scan.rs, is_end_line() uses eq_ignore_ascii_case (line 97). The decode.rs approach is correct but opaque — why allocate for a 3-byte comparison? A reader has to reason through whether the lowercasing is necessary (it is, for correctness with 'END' or 'End') but could use eq_ignore_ascii_case directly. No cross-crate doc explains why the two paths use different idioms for the same check.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the lowercase-Vec + == b"end" pattern in decode.rs with .eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"end"), consistent with scan.rs.
close_reason: Replaced lowercase-Vec + == b'end' with .eq_ignore_ascii_case(b'end') in uuencoding/src/decode.rs (done as part of MIME-gcz.9)
